title: Type 2 Diabetes: Treatment Intensification and Add-On Therapy

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with type 2 diabetes above their HbA1c target on initial therapy: optimise first, then choose add-on drugs by comorbidity, start insulin when criteria are met, and review or stop drugs. Checked against SDCPG 2021 (pp. 28, 31, 42, 46–48) and NICE NG28 (updated 18 Feb 2026, sections 1.5–1.8, 1.19–1.31). Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Each new non-insulin class added to initial therapy lowers HbA1c by about 0.7–1.0% (SDCPG p. 47). SGLT-2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists are chosen for cardiovascular and kidney benefit as much as for glucose lowering (NG28 section 1.13 preamble). Insulin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones and glinides add weight; DPP-4 inhibitors and metformin are weight neutral; GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT-2 inhibitors lower weight (SDCPG p. 42). Sulfonylureas and insulin raise hypoglycaemia and fall risk, most importantly in frailty (NG28 1.31.2). Insulin is indicated whatever the diabetes duration once the criteria are met (SDCPG p. 48).

symptoms: Persisting or new polyuria and polydipsia despite treatment (SDCPG p. 47).
Hypoglycaemic symptoms on a sulfonylurea or insulin (NG28 1.31.2).
Weight loss or weight gain since starting treatment (SDCPG p. 42).
physicalSigns: HbA1c at or above 58 mmol/mol (7.5%) on the initial regimen (NG28 1.5.8).
Injection-site problems that reduce insulin delivery (SDCPG p. 48).
redFlags: HbA1c above 10%, glucose consistently above 300 mg/dL or catabolic features: do not delay insulin (SDCPG p. 48).
BMI below 18.5 kg/m²: stop GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide (NG28 1.24.3).
Recurrent or severe hypoglycaemia or impaired awareness on multiple daily insulin: offer intermittently scanned CGM (NG28 1.7.1).
Response that does not fit type 2 diabetes: revisit the diagnosis (NG28 1.22.3).
precipitants: Poor adherence, wrong dose or formulation, or diet drift (NG28 1.22.2).
Intercurrent illness or starting oral or intravenous corticosteroids (NG28 1.6.3–1.6.4).
New cardiovascular disease, heart failure or kidney disease (NG28 1.27.1, 1.30.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Check doses, formulation, adherence and diet before changing drugs (NG28 1.22.2).
Disturbed red-cell turnover or abnormal haemoglobin: use fructosamine or total glycated haemoglobin (NG28 1.5.3; SDCPG p. 31).
Short-term capillary monitoring and review when steroids start or illness occurs (NG28 1.6.3–1.6.4).
Unexpected response should prompt a diagnosis review (NG28 1.22.3).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: At or above 58 mmol/mol (7.5%) on the initial regimen: intensify and aim for 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) (NG28 1.5.8).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Measure every 3–6 months until stable on unchanging therapy, then every 6 months (NG28 1.5.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Optimise before adding
actions: Check adverse effects, doses, formulations, adherence and diet advice before changing drugs (NG28 1.22.2).
Check that HbA1c is valid and that the diagnosis still fits (NG28 1.5.3, 1.22.3).
Make the change as a shared decision (NG28 1.22.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose the add-on by profile
actions: SDCPG: for ASCVD, heart failure or CKD prefer a GLP-1 receptor agonist or SGLT-2 inhibitor; otherwise choose by side effects, price and patient preference (p. 47).
NICE: follow the profile branches below (NG28 1.25–1.31).
Add a DPP-4 inhibitor; if contraindicated, not tolerated or ineffective add a sulfonylurea, pioglitazone or insulin (NG28 1.25.1).
Add a DPP-4 inhibitor; if not suitable add a sulfonylurea or insulin (NG28 1.26.1).
If it develops after starting treatment, add subcutaneous semaglutide up to 1 mg weekly (NG28 1.27.1). For glucose, add a sulfonylurea, pioglitazone or insulin (1.27.2).

branches.condition: Early onset or living with obesity
actions: Consider a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide; for obesity only after at least 3 months of initial therapy (NG28 1.28.1, 1.29.2).
Consider a DPP-4 inhibitor, then pioglitazone, a sulfonylurea (eGFR 30 or more) or insulin (NG28 1.30.1).
Consider a DPP-4 inhibitor, then pioglitazone, a sulfonylurea or insulin; sulfonylureas and insulin raise hypoglycaemia and fall risk (NG28 1.31.1–1.31.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Combination rules
actions: Introduce one drug at a time and check tolerability and effect (NG28 1.20.1).
Start a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide once the SGLT-2 inhibitor is at its maximum tolerated dose (NG28 1.20.2).
Do not offer a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide together with a DPP-4 inhibitor (NG28 1.24.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Start or add insulin
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as criteria are met
actions: Criteria: HbA1c above target on 3 or more agents for 3 months or more, HbA1c above 10%, glucose consistently above 300 mg/dL, severe weight loss or osmotic symptoms (SDCPG p. 48).
Basal insulin 0.1–0.2 units/kg/day if HbA1c is below 8%, 0.2–0.3 units/kg/day if above 8%; titrate by 2 units every third day to the fasting target (SDCPG p. 48).
Add prandial insulin with the largest meal if post-meal glucose is high despite fasting at target: start 4–5 units or 10% of the basal dose; titrate by 1–2 units or 10% every 2–3 days (SDCPG p. 48).
Premixed insulin: at least twice and at most three times daily (SDCPG p. 48). Review every 2 weeks until self-monitored glucose is near target (SDCPG p. 48).
Offer intermittently scanned CGM on multiple daily insulin with recurrent or severe hypoglycaemia, impaired awareness, inability to self-monitor, or a need for 8 or more checks a day (NG28 1.7.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Review and stop
actions: Consider continuing drugs that helped reach the glycaemic and weight targets (NG28 1.24.1).
Consider continuing an SGLT-2 inhibitor for cardiovascular or kidney benefit even if it does not help the glucose target (NG28 1.24.2).
Stop a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide if BMI falls below 18.5 kg/m² or if there is no glycaemic benefit and no cardiovascular indication (NG28 1.24.3–1.24.4).
In frailty, keep the smallest effective number of drugs at the lowest effective dose (NG28 1.19.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: HbA1c every 3–6 months until stable, then every 6 months (NG28 1.5.1).
Do not offer routine self-monitoring unless on insulin, hypoglycaemic episodes, hypoglycaemic drugs while driving or operating machinery, or pregnancy (NG28 1.6.2).
Check vitamin B12 periodically on prolonged metformin (SDCPG p. 46).

teaching.scope: Adults with type 2 diabetes above their HbA1c target on initial therapy: optimise first, then choose add-on drugs by comorbidity, start insulin when criteria are met, and review or stop drugs. Checked against SDCPG 2021 (pp. 28, 31, 42, 46–48) and NICE NG28 (updated 18 Feb 2026, sections 1.5–1.8, 1.19–1.31).
learningObjectives: Optimise before intensifying, then pick an add-on that fits the person's comorbidity.
Start insulin on time using the Saudi criteria and doses.
pitfalls: Adding drugs without checking adherence, dose and diet first.
Using a sulfonylurea or insulin in a frail person without weighing hypoglycaemia and falls.
Continuing a GLP-1 receptor agonist after BMI falls below 18.5 kg/m².
keyPoints: Add one drug at a time and recheck HbA1c in 3 months.
Never combine a GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide with a DPP-4 inhibitor.
Do not delay insulin when HbA1c is above 10%, glucose is above 300 mg/dL or there are catabolic features.

patientEducation: Explain why a second or third drug may be needed and which side effects to report.
Teach injection technique and site rotation before insulin starts (SDCPG p. 48).
lifestyleAndDiet: Revisit diet and activity advice at every intensification (NG28 1.22.2).
Recheck weight and BMI at each visit (SDCPG p. 42).
mdtReferrals: Diabetes specialist team if HbA1c stays above target on 3 agents or insulin is started.
Dietitian; ophthalmology review before rapid HbA1c reduction (NG28 1.20.2 refers to the diabetic retinopathy guideline).
dischargeCriteria: New regimen tolerated with no hypoglycaemia.
Insulin technique checked and titration plan written.
Next HbA1c booked for about 3 months.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review every 2 weeks while titrating insulin until readings are near target (SDCPG p. 48); HbA1c 3 months after any change, then every 3–6 months until stable (NG28 1.5.1).
